outcome: Cord blood Total Nucleated Cell (TNC) content
cohort: The study participants consisted of 2583 umbilical cord blood units (CBUs) and their associated maternal and neonatal clinic laboratory data obtained from the InScientiaFides cord blood bank.
finding: The study identified a predictive model where male babies, gestational age lower than 39 weeks, cesarean delivery, and TNC content higher than 3.44 x 10^8 are significantly associated with a higher CD34+ cell content in cord blood units.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery positively affects CBU volume and is a significant factor, alongside male gender and gestational age lower than 39 weeks, in a predictive model for higher cord blood CD34+ content.
cross-section timing: At the time of birth/cord blood collection
birth_weight: Measured and found to have a positive correlation with CB TNC content, CD34+ content, and CBU volume.
gest_age: Measured and found to have a positive correlation with CB TNC content, with gestational age lower than 39 weeks being a predictor for higher CD34+ content.
